source.title: 1-Bend 3-D Orthogonal Box-Drawings: Two Open Problems Solved

accepted.question_text: For the complete graph K_n, must every three-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing in which each edge route has at most one bend have total volume Ω(n^3)?

evidence.quote: Two open problems for such drawings are: (1) Does every drawing of Kn have volume Ω(n3)?
Since Kn = Gn,n−1, any 1-bend drawing of Kn has volume Ω(n3), which answers the first open problem mentioned above.

accepted.question_text: For the complete graph K_n, does there exist a three-dimensional orthogonal cube-drawing in which each edge route has at most one bend and each vertex is represented by a cube whose surface area is O(n), equivalently a degree-restricted 1-bend cube-drawing for K_n?

evidence.quote: (2) Is there a drawing of Kn for which additionally the vertices are represented by cubes with surface O(n)?
Hence, the question was posed whether Kn has a degree-restricted 1-bend cube-drawing.
In particular, Kn does not have a 1-bend degree-restricted cube-drawing. (This settles the second open problem mentioned above.)

accepted.question_text: Does every graph admit a three-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing in which each edge route has at most one bend and the total volume is O(Δ n^2), where n is the number of vertices and Δ is the maximum degree?

evidence.quote: Does every graph have a 1-bend drawing of volume O(∆n2)?

accepted.question_text: Can the edge set of every graph be partitioned into O(Δ) matchings together with a suitable ordering of the vertices so that, in the resulting three-dimensional orthogonal 1-bend construction, each matching can be drawn in its own Z-plane without crossings?

evidence.quote: Can a graph be split in O(∆) matchings such that for a suitable vertex order all matchings are without crossing?

accepted.question_text: If every graph can be decomposed into O(Δ) crossing-free matchings in the sense described above, does it follow that every graph has a three-dimensional orthogonal 1-bend drawing of volume O(m n), where m is the number of edges and n is the number of vertices?

evidence.quote: If the answer is yes, does every graph have a 1-bend drawing of volume O(mn)?

accepted.question_text: Does every graph admit a three-dimensional orthogonal cube-drawing in which each edge route has at most one bend and the total volume is O(Δ^3 n), where n is the number of vertices and Δ is the maximum degree?

evidence.quote: Does every graph have a 1-bend cube-drawing of volume O(∆3n)?

accepted.question_text: If every graph has a three-dimensional orthogonal 1-bend cube-drawing of volume O(Δ^3 n), does it follow that every graph has a three-dimensional orthogonal 1-bend drawing of volume O(Δ^2 m), where m is the number of edges and Δ is the maximum degree?

evidence.quote: If the answer is yes, does every graph have a 1-bend drawing of volume O(∆2m)?

accepted.question_text: For three-dimensional orthogonal graph drawings in which each edge route has at most two bends, what is the correct asymptotic lower bound on the required volume; in particular, is the lower bound Ω(Δ n^2), as in the 1-bend case?

evidence.quote: What is the correct lower bound for 2-bend drawings? There are drawings of size O(n3) for Kn [BSWW99] as well as O(∆n2) for all graphs [Bie98]. Is the lower bound Ω(∆n2), as for the 1-bend case?

accepted.question_text: For three-dimensional orthogonal graph drawings in which each edge route has at most three bends, what is the correct asymptotic lower bound on the required volume; specifically, for graphs of maximum degree Δ on n vertices, does every graph admit such a drawing of volume O(Δ n^1.5), which would match the known Ramanujan-graph lower bound Ω(Δ n^1.5)?

evidence.quote: What is the correct lower bound for 3-bend drawings? There are drawings of size O(n2.5) for Kn [BSWW99], and this is optimal [BSWW99]. For Ramanujan-graphs, the lower bound is Ω(∆n1.5) [BTW01], but it is not known whether every graph has a 3-bend drawing of volume O(∆n1.5).
